h1: Retaining Wall Repair in Woodstock, Ontario
intro: The block walls we get called to repair around Woodstock most often show the same problem: individual blocks separating or bulging near the base, which almost always traces back to blocked or missing drainage.

sections.heading: Why Block Walls Separate in Woodstock

blocks.text: When drainage stone behind a block wall gets clogged with fine soil, or was never installed with enough depth, water pressure has nowhere to go but against the blocks. Over a few seasons, that pressure pushes the lower courses outward, separating joints and eventually bulging the wall face.
Sandy soil pockets around Woodstock can also let a wall's base erode if the original footing wasn't compacted to sufficient depth, leading to settlement rather than bulging.

items.title: Site visit
items.text: We inspect the wall, checking for how far out of plumb it has moved and where drainage is failing.

items.title: Root cause diagnosis
items.text: We identify whether the issue is drainage, base settlement, or a combination.

items.title: Written quote
items.text: Detailed scope and cost provided before any work starts.

blocks.text: Depending on severity, repair may involve dismantling and rebuilding the affected section with new drainage stone and geogrid, or a more limited fix if the damage is caught early. We never recommend a full rebuild when a targeted repair will hold.
Minor drainage-related repairs typically run $500 to $2,000. More extensive rebuilding ranges from $3,000 to $15,000 or more depending on wall length and damage extent.

Once a Woodstock wall is repaired with proper drainage in place, ongoing maintenance is minimal. A quick seasonal check after heavy rain is usually enough to catch a developing problem before it becomes a repair call again.
See /retaining-wall-maintenance-tips for the specific things worth checking through the year.
Where possible, we plan repair excavation to minimize disruption to established plantings around a Woodstock wall, though some disturbance is often unavoidable near the repair area itself.

faqs.q: Why is my block wall bulging near the bottom?
faqs.a: Usually water pressure building up behind the lower courses because drainage stone is clogged or insufficient. We diagnose the specific cause on the free site visit.

faqs.q: Can a bulging block wall be fixed without tearing it all out?
faqs.a: Often the affected section can be dismantled and rebuilt with corrected drainage, without touching the rest of the wall, if the damage is localized.

faqs.q: How urgent is a leaning retaining wall?
faqs.a: Walls that are visibly moving should be assessed promptly, especially if they're near a structure, driveway or walkway.

faqs.q: Do you offer free assessments for wall repair in Woodstock?
faqs.a: Yes, every repair starts with a free, no-obligation site visit and written quote.

faqs.q: What can I do to prevent needing another repair down the road?
faqs.a: Keep drainage outlets clear of debris and check the wall after major rain events. Catching small issues early avoids larger repairs later.

faqs.q: Will repair work damage my existing landscaping?
faqs.a: We minimize disruption where possible, though some disturbance near the repair area is often unavoidable. We'll discuss expectations before starting.

faqs.q: Is it worth getting a second opinion before committing to a repair?
faqs.a: We welcome it. Every assessment comes with a written explanation of the cause and scope, which you're free to compare against another quote before deciding how to proceed.
